content: Burp models WebSockets as a distinct 'WebSockets history' tab (table of messages), separate from the HTTP proxy history, keyed to the upgrade handshake exchange; a Repeater WS tab lets you resend individual messages on the still-open channel. mitmproxy (v6+) attaches a  attribute to the HTTPFlow that performed the Upgrade handshake; that attribute holds a list of WebSocketMessage objects (mitmproxy reassembles fragmented frames into single messages, always stored as bytes to avoid str/bytes confusion). Both tools treat the handshake as one exchange and the frame stream as a child list hung off it, not as independent request/response exchanges.
